title: Is Now a Good Time to Buy? Middle Tennessee Numbers
description: Is now a good time to buy a home in Middle Tennessee? A plain look at current Nashville-area market data, mortgage rates and the questions that matter.
keyword: is now a good time to buy
body:
People ask me this question more than any other, and I understand why. A home is a big purchase, and the headlines rarely agree with each other.

I can't tell you where prices or rates will go, and nobody else can either. What I can do is show you what the current local numbers say, what they mean in plain terms, and how to weigh them against your own situation.

## What the local numbers show

{{img:0}}

Start with the Nashville metro area. According to the Redfin Data Center, for the four weeks ending 2026-09-27, the median sale price was $462,304. The median home spent 68 days on the market, and homes sold for 97.8% of their list price on average. There were 2,489 homes sold in that period.

A slightly longer view tells a similar story. For Nashville as of 2026-08-31 (Redfin, rolling 3 months), the median sale price was $477,500, down 0.1% from a year earlier. Median days on market was 64, the average sale-to-list ratio was 97.6%, and there were 4,850 active listings.

In plain terms: prices are roughly flat compared with last year, homes are taking a couple of months to sell, and the typical buyer is paying a little under the asking price. That is a description of the recent past, not a forecast.

You can see more local figures on our [market data page for the I-65 corridor](/market-data), and you can browse the source yourself at the [Redfin Data Center](https://www.redfin.com/news/data-center/).

## Months of supply, explained

Months of supply is how long it would take to sell every active listing at the current pace of sales. Under 4 months generally favors sellers. Between 4 and 6 months is considered balanced. Over 6 months generally favors buyers.

Redfin shows Nashville at 5.3 months of supply (as of 2026-08-31), and 5.4 months for the four weeks ending 2026-09-27. That sits in the balanced range, toward the upper end.

Other sources point the same direction. The overall rating in the data we pulled for this post is "leans toward buyers." The Zillow Market Temperature Index for Nashville reads 44, and it has moved down 6 points over 3 months, which Zillow describes as cooling. Realtor.com's hotness score for Davidson County is 16.6 out of 100. You can read how each is built at Zillow Research and [Realtor.com Research](https://www.realtor.com/research/data/).

Two cautions. These are metro-wide or county-wide figures, and a single street or price range can behave very differently. And a cooling reading describes what already happened. It doesn't promise what comes next.

## What the mortgage rate does to the picture

{{img:1}}

Price is only part of the cost. The 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.28% for the week of 2026-10-01, according to Freddie Mac via FRED. You can check the latest weekly reading at the Freddie Mac 30-year rate series on FRED.

A higher rate raises the monthly payment on any given loan amount, so it can change what price range fits your budget more than the sale price itself does. Rates can also change from week to week, and the rate you are offered depends on your credit, down payment, loan type and lender.

The easiest way to see this for yourself is to run a few scenarios in our [mortgage calculator](/mortgage-calculator). Try different prices, down payments and rates, and see which monthly numbers you are comfortable with.

## Questions that matter more than the headline

A market reading can tell you about conditions. It can't tell you whether buying fits your life. These are the questions I would work through instead:

- **How long do you expect to stay?** Buying and selling both carry costs. Closing costs typically run 2 to 4 percent of the purchase price, plus earnest money and moving costs.
- **What monthly payment is comfortable?** Include property taxes, insurance and, on a conventional loan with under 20 percent down, private mortgage insurance.
- **How much cushion will you have after closing?** Repairs, moving and furnishing add up quickly.
- **Is your job and income stable right now?** Lenders look at this, and changing jobs or opening new credit between application and closing can cause problems.
- **Is there a reason tied to a date?** A lease ending or a relocation can matter more than any market chart.

If your answers point toward buying, the market data can help you set expectations on negotiation and timing. If they don't, the data is not a reason to go ahead.

## Getting your financing in order first

Whatever you decide, it helps to know your real numbers. A pre-qualification is a quick estimate based on what you tell a lender. A pre-approval goes further: the lender reviews your documents and credit before issuing a letter. A pre-approval letter is still not a final loan commitment, since final approval depends on the appraisal, underwriting and your finances staying the same until closing.

The CFPB encourages borrowers to get Loan Estimates from more than one lender and compare them, because rates and fees can differ. The Loan Estimate is a standard three-page form, so side-by-side comparison is straightforward. Credit-scoring models generally treat several mortgage inquiries made within a short period as a single inquiry, but ask each lender how it works for your situation. The [CFPB Owning a Home guides](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/) walk through this in detail.

You choose your own lender. Banks, credit unions, mortgage brokers and online lenders all make home loans. Also ask whether a lender takes part in programs from the [Tennessee Housing Development Agency](https://www.thda.org), which offers home loan programs through participating lenders.

## Where this leaves you

Here is what I can say honestly. Recent local data shows flat year-over-year prices, homes selling a bit under asking, supply in the balanced range, and a mortgage rate of 7.28%. Those facts may give buyers a little more room to negotiate than they had in tighter markets. They also come with a higher financing cost. Whether that adds up to the right move depends on your budget, your timeline and the specific home.

If you want to talk it through, you can [get matched with homes and a call with me](/buy#form). When you fill out the form, I schedule a call and we will be talking within the next 48 hours. If you would rather ask a question first, you can [contact me directly](/contact). There is no pressure either way.

faq.q: Is now a good time to buy a home in Nashville?
faq.a: It depends on your budget, timeline and plans. As of 2026-08-31, Redfin shows Nashville at 5.3 months of supply, which is in the balanced range, with a median sale price down 0.1% from a year earlier. Those figures describe recent conditions and are not a prediction.

faq.q: What is the current 30-year mortgage rate?
faq.a: Freddie Mac, via FRED, reported a 30-year fixed rate of 7.28% for the week of 2026-10-01. The rate you are offered depends on your credit, down payment, loan type and lender.

faq.q: Are Nashville home prices going up or down?
faq.a: Redfin reported a Nashville median sale price of $477,500 as of 2026-08-31, down 0.1% from a year earlier. That is a look back at the past year and does not predict where prices go next.

faq.q: What does months of supply mean?
faq.a: It is how long it would take to sell every active listing at the current pace of sales. Under 4 months favors sellers, 4 to 6 months is balanced, and over 6 months favors buyers.
